notes: Draft 2026-11-14, written from model knowledge only: no model run, no web lookup; every fact is asserted, not measured. Countries are LANG keys of twohop-20261113/ext/gen_ext.py (which already include Indonesia and Iran); capital = CAP2 spelling (Ukraine = 'Kiev'). chain lists the latent entities from the descriptor to the person whose birthplace is asked; the capital and country are the last two latents. So d5 = 2 chain entities + city + country = 4 latents; d6 = 3 + 2 = 5. A script asserts these counts and that the descriptor never contains the capital, country or language string (other countries' names may appear as distractors and are flagged in doubts). Extra field 'prompt' = the d-panel prompt string. Caveats: (1) items marked 'shortcut' have an earlier person born in the same capital, so a model that skips a hop still scores; keep them apart or use them as a control. (2) '-of-adaptation' items whose source and adaptation share a title may collapse to one latent (effective depth one lower). (3) d6 'adaptation-by-author' items use a year plus author to make the work latent; uniqueness rests on that year. (4) Surface variants of one chain (Strauss: Blue Danube / Fledermaus; Plato/Socrates teacher chains; Polanski x3; Hitchcock; Kurosawa) are not independent items. (5) Thailand, Turkey and Bulgaria have no items; I found no well-known capital-born person reachable by a unique 2-3 hop relation. Countries are uneven: Austria, France, Britain and Japan dominate. native_city: all non-capitals in LANG countries; the capitals in the request (Praha, Wien, Lisboa, Kobenhavn, Warszawa, Moskva) and Bruxelles (Belgium not in LANG) are excluded. 'differs_from_english' = True when the native form is a different word or has diacritics/inflection that change tokenisation; same-name rows are controls. Weak 'differs' rows: Hannover/Hanover, Marseille/Marseilles, Lyon/Lyons, Porto/Oporto, Odesa/Odessa, Malmo, Lodz (spelling or diacritics only).
